lawyer:
AKM Rabiul Hassan with MM Shafiullah, Advocates —For the Petitioner. 
Abdul Quiyum, Senior Advocate with Md Mahbubur Rahman, Advocates—For the Opposite Party No. 1.
parties:
Feroz Shai -------- Defendant-Respondent-Petitioner
VS
Habibur Rahman Khalifa and others Plaintiffs-Appellants ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-5-2014 (decree signed on 22-5-2014), passed by the Additional District Judge, Madaripur, in Title Appeal No.76 of 2012, allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 29-7-2012 (decree signed on 2-8-2012), passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Madaripur, in Title Suit No.77 of 2011, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. The application for rejecting the revisional application filed by the opposite party-applicant is taken up for disposal alongwith this Rule. 

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that, admittedly one Abdul Kader Khalifa, the father of the plaintiff-appellant was the owner of 92.50 acres of land in the concerned Mouza that includes the suit property as well. The case of the plaintiff is that, Abdul Kader Khalifa died leaving the plaintiff and the defendant Nos. 3-8 and their mother Zobeda Begum as his heirs. After the death of Zobeda Begum, the plaintiff and the defendant Nos. 3-8 were her heirs and accordingly the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the concerned Jama. The plaintiff admits that, the defendant No. 2 Md Younus Takukder was a co-sharer by purchase in the concerned Jama. However, the further case of the plaintiff is that, the plaintiff was enjoying the suit property along with other co-sharers, the defendant No. 2 (co-sharer by purchase) and defendant Nos. 3-8, brothers and sister, i.e. the co-sharer by inheritance. The further case of the plaintiff is that, the defendant No. 2, Md Younus Talukder, sold 12 decimals of land, secretly, by a registered deed No.4760 dated 13-12-2009. It has also been stated that, when Motiur Rahman. Howlader, brother of defendant No. 1 (purchaser) was filling earth in the suit property on 25-1-2011 and having seen this, the plaintiff asked Motiur Rahman Howlader as to why he was filling earth and then he came to know about the fact of sale of the suit property, on 25-1-2011 and at once, he, (plaintiff) shouted then and there that he has right to pre-emption in the suit property. Having heard this shout, local people, namely-Badsha Khalifa, Mozammel Khalifa, Motaleb Mollah, Mozazzel Matbor came forward, approached to the suit property, and then the plaintiff again demanded, keeping them as witnesses, that, he has right to pre-emption of the suit property and accordingly, he has filed this suit claiming that, he had already performed the formalities of Talab-e-Muasibat and Talab-e-Eshad. 

3. The defendant No. 1 Feroz Shai appeared in the suit and contested by filing written objection. His plain case is that, the plaintiff's father Abdul Kader Khalifa sold 24 decimals of land by deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994 to Md Younus Talukder (defendant No. 2) and one Abdul Jalil. The buyer Md Younus Talukder, thereafter, got separate mutation and separate Jama in his own name, in respect of 12 decimals of land, Md Younus Talukder by a registered sale deed No. 4760 dated 13-12-2009 sold his 12 decimals of land to the defendant No. 1. Besides, the plaintiff's had 30 decimals of land adjacent to the suit property and long before he had developed the said land (total 42 decimals) by filling earth and had constructed huts and installed Tube-well and has peacefully possessed the same with the knowledge of all. Further case of the defendant is that, the plaintiff has admitted in Title Suit No. 42 of 2011 that, they had no right in the suit property and that, in a proceeding, drawn under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Court of Magistrate found that, the defendant No. 1 (purchaser) had been peacefully possessing the suit property. His further case is that, the plaintiff's father Abdul Kader Khalifa having sold the suit property to defendant No. 2, Md Younus Talukder, by a registered deed 1227 dated 3-4-1994, and Younus Talukder having opened a mutation khatian and getting separate Jama in his name, the plaintiff had ceased to be a co-sharer in the 12 decimals of suit Plot since the date of deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994. Hence, the defendant has purchased 12 decimals of suit property by a registered deed and the plaintiff is not a co-sharer. Moreover, the defendant also asserts that, the case of the plaintiff is barred by limitation. 

4. In order to prove the case, the plaintiff had produced and proved some documents, marked as Exhibit 1 and 2 series, 3 and 4 and the defendant has produced and proved some documentary evidence, marked as Exhibit "Ka" and "Kha", as well as both sides had given oral evidence to support their respective cases. 

5. The trial court, after hearing the parties and having assessed the evidence on record, dismissed the suit by it's judgment and decree dated 29-7-2012 (decree signed on 2-8-2012). 

6. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.76 of 2012 (as appellant) before the District Judge, Madaripur, which was heard by the Additional District Judge, Madaripur, who has allowed the appeal, vide judgment and decree dated 18-5-2014 (decree signed on 22-5-2014) and thereby reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate court, the defendant-respondent-petitioner has filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule. 

8. Learned Advocate Mr AKM Rabiul Hassan and Mr MM Shafiullah appeared for the defendant-respondent-petitioner. Mr Rabiul Hassan, having placed the revisional application, first of all submits that, admittedly the suit property belonged to Abdul Kader Khalifa, father of the plaintiff alongwith other non-suit properties of the concerned Mouza. This Abdul Kader Khalifa, by a registered deed No. 1227 dated 03-4-1994, had sold total 24 decimals of land to Md Younus Talukder and to one Abdul Jalil and they got separate mutation and separate Jama in their respective names recording 12 decimals of land, proportionately, pursuant to deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994, but the plaintiff did not challenge the said deed. Thereafter, he proceeds on that, the brother and sisters of the plaintiffs are claiming to be co-sharers (defendant Nos. 3-8) of the concerned Jama. The learned Advocate then continues that, the plaintiff had ceased to be co-sharers in the 12 decimals of suit land since their father Abdul Kader Khalifa had transferred this 12 decimals of land to Md Younus Talukder (defendant No. 2) by a registered deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994 and Md Younus Talukder, thereafter, got a separate mutation khatian and also got the Jama in respect of that 12 decimals of land purchased by him. Therefore, the plaintiff has ceased to be a co-sharer, since the date of transfer i.e. from 3-4-1994 and they had no locus-standi to file this suit. He next submits that, the trial court has rightly found that, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation under article 10 of schedule 1 of the Limitation Act. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has referred to Exhibit "Kha", which is the certified copy of the plaint, filed by the plaintiff Habibur Rahman Khalifa against the said Motiur Rahman Howlader and others, seeking permanent injunction in respect of the same property, including the suit Plot No. 403, under khatian No. 228 of Mouza Mozafforpur. In the judgment, passed in the previous Title Suit No.42 of 2011, the court has recorded that, the plaintiff's father has sold 24 decimals of land from Plot No. 403 to Md Younus Talukder and Abdul Jalil by a registered deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994 and thereafter Md Younus Talukder has sold his 12 decimals of land to the defendant No. 1 Feroz Shai, by a registered deed No. 4760 dated 13-12-2009. As such, the learned Advocate points out that, the same plaintiff was aware about the sale deed No. 4760 dated 13-12-2009, since the Title Suit was filed by him, on 24-2-2011, i.e. long before filing of the present suit for pre-emption on 5-4-2011. But, the plaintiff has deliberately suppressed the fact of filing the previous Title Suit No. 42 of 2011 (seeking permanent injunction). The learned Advocate next submits that, the finding of the trial court that, the suit is barred by limitation under article 10 schedule 1 of the Limitation Act is absolutely lawful and that, these plaintiffs have resorted to fraud in filing the instant suit by suppressing the fact of their acquiring knowledge of the sale to the defendant No. 1, long before 25-1-2011 (the alleged date of Talab-E-Muasibat). The plaintiff is not a credible one, while his witnesses, i.e. PWs 1 and 3 are his uncle and his cultivator respectively, who are apparently partisan witnesses and that, the plaintiff could not prove his case of Talab-E-Muasibat and Talab-E-Eshad. Rather, the trial court has rightly passed the judgment and decree relying upon the deposition of P.W. Nos. 1-3 and having assessed the entire evidence on record in its proper perspective. On the contrary, the appellate court has failed to notice the fact proved by the Exhibit "Ka" and "Kha" and the deed No. 4760 dated 13-12-2009, whereby the defendant No. 1 (Pre-emptee) has derived title of 12 decimals of land from Md Younus Talukder, who is not the predecessor of the plaintiff and admittedly, the plaintiff is not heir of Md Younus Talukder. The defendant-appellant-petitioner purchased the suit property from Md Younus Talukder, which is the subject of separate .lama, he also points out. Moreover, the appellate court remained totally silent about the Exhibit "Kha", (Judgment of the previous suit for permanent injunction filed by the same plaintiff) and in which he failed to get the decree of permanent injunction in respect of the self-same suit property, which has been deliberately suppressed from the knowledge of the court by the plaintiff (pre-emptor),at the time of filing of the instant pre-emption case, and the appellate court has thus failed to perform its duty to assess the material evidence independently dispassionately. Moreso, the appellate court has totally overlooked the findings of the trial court about the contradictions found in the deposition of the witnesses of the plaintiff as recorded in the trial court's judgment, and that, the plaintiff could not mention the time of filling of the earth on 25-1-2011, while the PW 2 and 3 contradicts each other about the time at which the plaintiff allegedly shouted declaring his right of pre-emption and about the numbers of Truck etc. The learned Advocate submits that, the appellate court, without giving any cogent reason, has reversed the findings of the trial court. Therefore, the finding of the appellate court is totally perverse and clearly amounts to misreading and non-reading of the evidence, while it has made out a 3rd case that, the transaction is benami transaction and for all these reasons, the learned Advocate submits that, the judgment of the appellant court is shockingly perverse and there are misreading and non-reading of the evidence in passing its judgment, hence, the same are liable to be reversed. He argues that, the plaintiff has also failed to prove the case of Talab-E-Muasibat and Talab-E-Eshad as has been rightly pointed out by the trial court, which is very essential prerequisite for claiming the right of pre-emption under the Muhammadan Law. The learned Advocate, in support of his contention, has referred to a decision, reported in 21 DLR page 211 between Md Lokman Mondal vs Amir Ali Mondal and others. Moreover, the plaintiff did not say that he needs a prior demand i.e. Talab-E-Muasibat and Talab-E-Eshad and on this ground alone, the findings of the appellate court may kindly be reversed. 

9. Learned Senior Advocate Mr Abdul Quiyum and learned Advocate Mr Md Mahbubur Rahman appeared on behalf of the opposite party No. 1. The main contention of the learned Advocates is that, the appeal filed by the defendant No. 1 i.e. the present petitioner was incompetent because his brother Motiur Rahman Howlader, although appeared before the trial court and had filed the written objection on behalf of the defendant No. 1, Feroz Shai, but, this Motiur Rahman Howlader did not have any power of attorney as required under the provisions of rule 2(a) of Order 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Mr Quiyum has argued at length on this point and submits that, the defendant No. 1 has not been represented in this case by a competent person. Therefore, the trial court ought not to have accepted his appearance and the appellate court ought to have arrived at the finding that, the appeal was not competent, since it was not filed by Feroz Shai. The further contention of the learned Advocate is that, the appellate court, as the last court of fact, has rightly assessed the evidence on record and found that, the plaintiff has rightly proved the Talab-E-Muasibat and Talab-E-Eshad as required under the Muhammadan Law and the appellate court has also found that, the suit was not barred by limitation and on these specific findings, the appellate court has reversed the findings of the trial court and has allowed the appeal. He next submits that, the appellate court has committed no error of law in passing the impugned judgment and decree, nor that has resulted in any error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Therefore, this Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged. 

10. The learned Advocate for the petitioner, in reply to the submissions of the learned Advocate for the opposite party, further submits that, as per description of parties given in the cause title to the plaint of Title Suit No.77 of 2011, Motiur Rahman Howlader is the brother and executants of Feroz Shai. He also submits that, the summon and notices were accordingly served upon Motiur Rahman Howlader, at the instance of the plaintiff, not upon Feroz Shai. He also points out that, this submission of the opposite party, rather cuts the very root of the plaintiff's case for the admitted position that, no summon or notice has been served upon the defendant No. 1 and the plaint was not properly presented or filed before the trial court and, as such, the entire proceedings is void ab-initio and is not maintainable. 

11. I have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, who have made their elaborate submissions, as noted hereinabove. 

12. From the examination of the plaint, I find that, the plaintiff has described the defendant as "ফিরোজ সাই, পিতা-মৃত অহেদ আলী হাওলাদার ওরফে অহেদ আলী সাই, সাং-মালেরকান্দি, পোঃ- সিকদারহাট, থানা+উপজেলা- শিবচর, জেলা-মাদারীপুর। পক্ষে-কার্য্যকারক মতিউর রহমান হাওলাদার, পিতা-মৃত অহেদ আলী হাওলাদার, সাং-মালেরকান্দি, পোঃ-সিকদারহাট, থানা-শিবচর, জেলা-মাদারীপুর। ক্রেতা-বিবাদী।” 

13. Therefore, apparently, the plaintiff has described and admitted Motiur Rahman Howlader as "কার্য্যকারক" (i.e. executants or agent) of the defendant No. 1 and the summons as well as the notices of appeal were served upon him, at the instance of the plaintiff. None of the courts below have found any difficulties, because Motiur Rahman Howlader is an admitted "কার্য্যকারক" as described by the plaintiffs. Based on this description, admitted position and narration of the plaintiff, both the courts below have proceeded to dispose of the matter before them, moreso, without any objection, that should have been raised (if there was any lawful scope) at the earliest opportunity. 

14. In my considered opinion, the provisions of rule 2(a) of Order 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not apply in this kind of case where the plaintiffs themselves have described the defendant-appellant-Motiur Rahman Howlader as the "কার্য্যকারক" (i.e. executant or agent) of the defendant No. 1-appellant. Moreover, the plaintiff cannot take advantage of his own conduct and is estoppels to deny his own description and admission of Motiur Rahman Howlader as the `Karjokarok' of his brother, defendant No. 1 (who was then staying at abroad). 

15. Besides, even if, it were found that, the courts below had committed an error of law in admitting Motiur Rahman Howlader as the executant of the plaintiff, then also I find that, such alleged error (though actually not) has not resulted in any erroneous decision, nor that had occasioned in the failure of justice in any manner. 

16. Next, 1 find that, the issue as to whether this plaintiff had any locus-standi to file the instant Title Suit No.77 of 2011, claiming pre-emption under the Muhammadan Law, has not been discussed by either of the courts below. It is to be recorded here that, the suit property, alongwith some other non-suit properties, belonged to the plaintiff's father Abdul Kader Khalifa, who, by a registered deed No. 1227 dated 03-4-1994, sold 24 decimals of land (that includes the 12 decimals of suit land) to Md Younus Talukder (i.e. the seller-defendant No. 2) and to Abdul Jalil Talukder, in equal shares. Thereafter, Md Younus Talukder, the defendant No. 2, has got his name mutated and his Jama was separated in respect of 12 decimals of land (the suit land), that falls into a separate Jama. As such, the 12 decimals of the suit property has ceased to be the part and parcel of the common Jama of Plot No. 403 of Mouza Mozafforpur and, admittedly, Md Younus Talukder was neither father, nor the predecessor of the plaintiff. So, the plaintiff has ceased to be a co-sharer in the suit property, sold by his father to Md Younus Talukder by registered deed 1227 dated 3-4-1994 and the suit property has, thereafter, become a property under separate Jama and khatian. As such, the plaintiffs had no locus-standi to file the Title Suit No.77 of 2011, seeking pre-emption in respect of the suit plot. 

17. Next, having turned my attention to the issue as to whether the suit is barred by limitation. I find that, the plaintiff knew about the transfer of the suit property to Md Younus Talukder, vide deed No.4760, 13-12-2009, as evident from the previous Title Suit No. 42 of 2011, filed by the plaintiff seeking permanent injunction in respect of the suit property and that suit was filed on 28-2-2011. The plaintiffs failed to get a decree of permanent injunction in that suit and then filed the instant suit, as the second chance. 

18. 1 find that, the conduct of the plaintiff, all along, is not fair. He is guilty of fraudulent suppressions of the fact of filing the previous suit for permanent injunction (Exhibit Kha), in respect of the self-same property. 

19. The plaintiff then, inspite of his having knowledge of his father's sale to Md Younus Talukder on 13-2-2009, has filed this instant frivolous, vexatious and ill-advised suit, and interestingly, tried to expose himself as an scholar about the formalities required to be performed for filing a pre-emption case under the provisions of Muhammadan Law, a practice which has almost lost into oblivion, since the pre-emption cases are now being filed, either under section 96 of the SAT Act, 1950 or under section 24 of the NAT Act, 1949. 

20. In view of the forgoing facts and circumstances, I am of the considered opinion that, the findings arrived at by the appellate court are based on misreading and non-reading of evidence as well as on misinterpretation of the oral evidence. The appellate court did not notice the lacuna and the contradictions in the deposition of PWs 1, 2 and 3, which has been rightly pointed out and duly recorded by the trial court in its judgment. Moreover, the appellate court, as the last court of fact, has neither considered the Exhibit "Kha" nor it has framed or decided the basic issue regarding the locus-standi of the plaintiffs in filing the instant suit. Hence, the findings of the appellate court should be reversed and the impugned judgment and decree should be set-aside, and those of the trial court should be upheld. 

21. This Rule has merit. 
Order 
In the result, the Rule is made absolute. 
The findings of the appellate court is hereby reversed and the judgment and decree dated 18-5-2014 (decree signed on 22-5-2014), passed by the Additional District Judge, Madaripur, in Title Appeal No.76 of 2012, is hereby set-aside and the judgment and decree dated 29-7-2012 (decree signed on 02-8-2012), passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Madaripur, in Title Suit No.77 of 2011, is hereby affirmed. 
Consequently, the application for rejecting the revisional application filed by the opposite party-applicant is also rejected. 
The order of stay granted earlier by this Court shall stand vacated. 
This is a fit case for awarding penal cost of Taka 1,00,000. However, taking a lenient view, cost is not imposed. 
Copies of this judgment be sent to the courts concerned alongwith the LCR at once. 

End.
